headline: ETFs took a provisional $525M on Oct 21, yet a −2.6% Nasdaq and $113 Brent pulled Bitcoin back into risk-off selling.
summary: Big-tech earnings revived AI-spending doubts and oil hit its highest since May, so BTC closed at the bottom of its 20-day range despite three straight days of ETF inflows. Funding swung from −4.48% back to 8.65% and longs were the ones liquidated on the way down, while the 10-year yield fell below 5% and October hike odds went to roughly zero. Bull day 14, no exit rule fired; watch whether ETF inflows continue, bids near 80,000 and the Oct 28 FOMC.

news.title: Meta −7.01%, Tesla −3.02% as AI-spending doubts return; Nasdaq closes −2.6%, S&P −1.2%; China's CSI 300 enters a bear market, 20% off its June high; Kospi −3.5%
news.read: BTC's 30-day correlation with Nasdaq is 0.597; it fell with tech and closed at the bottom of its 20-day range, just as it rose with tech two days earlier — risk appetite is driving the short term. Macro backdrop; the 200-day MA is still 10.5% below, so the market stage is unaffected.

news.title: US spot BTC ETFs took in $528.4M on Oct 21 (SoSoValue), IBIT +$235M, FBTC +$212.7M; Farside records $524.8M, about $1.075B over Oct 19–21
news.read: The two sources are 0.7% apart, so a provisional $524.8M (Farside basis) was recorded per the rules, to be overwritten by The Block. Three days of inflows is the strongest run since September, yet price closed lower and the Coinbase premium is −0.134%, meaning ETF buying was absorbed by other sellers. Only sustained inflows would show up in exchange supply and realized cap; no effect on the cycle call for now.

news.title: The US 10-year yield fell below 5% for the first time in over a month, to 4.945% intraday (−20bp on the day); CME FedWatch October hike odds dropped from 16% to roughly zero
news.read: Yields fell on a flight to safety, not easing; the site's FRED reading is still Oct 21's 5.13% with a 2.76% real yield and will update next issue. Higher odds of no hike on Oct 28 ease rate pressure on BTC, yet BTC still fell with stocks the same day. No effect on the market stage.

news.title: Brent rose $4.35 (+4.0%) to settle at $113.17, its highest since May 4; WTI settled at $99.47 after another Houthi attack on Saudi infrastructure and attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz
news.read: Oil feeds inflation and hike expectations, but this time yields fell on safe-haven buying, so the two partly offset; for BTC the main effect is weaker risk appetite. Background pressure; no effect on the market stage or exit framework.

news.title: BTC round-trips to 85,000: about $431M in 24-hour crypto liquidations, ~$173M of shorts on the climb, then $210M of the next 12 hours' $222M were longs (CoinGlass)
news.read: Consistent with funding swinging from −4.48% back to 8.65%: shorts were squeezed out, then the longs who chased were flushed, so leverage is shrinking on both sides. Modest size and short-term structure; no effect on the cycle call. A ~$186M bid wall sits at 80,000.

news.title: CoinDesk analysis: ETFs drew $1.08B in three days, but steep rallies since 2024 averaged about $235M a day; since Jul 1 the average is about $86M a day with no single day above $1B
news.read: Matches the site's numbers: the 7 complete trading days Oct 12–20 total only +$322M, under $50M a day; the three strong days need to continue to reach rally-era pace. A flows reading; no effect on the cycle call.

news.title: Chinese prosecutors seek to confiscate more than 61,800 BTC tied to a $5.7B (40B+ yuan) fraud; the coins were seized in the UK, where the High Court ruled Chinese law governs victims' claims
news.read: The coins have been frozen for years; whether, when and by whom they are disposed of still depends on further UK hearings, so they will not hit the market soon. Exchange supply −1.63% over 30 days is unrelated. Long-term potential supply; no effect on the cycle call.

news.title: JPMorgan: the Senate failed to advance the Clarity Act in September and passage this year is unlikely; SEC and OCC moves partly offset it, but could be reversed within two years if a Democrat wins the White House in 2028
news.read: The framework rests on agency action rather than law, so long-term political risk remains; no direct site indicator, and ETF flows are unaffected. Medium-to-long-term regulatory backdrop; no effect on the cycle call.

findings.title: Short-term buyers cashed in on the drop; no panic selling
findings.lean_why: Profit-taking supply hit the market on a down day; it is not panic selling and does not mean the cycle has turned.
findings.what: Short-term holders realized 7,940 BTC of profit (10/22, 1-year percentile 98.9, the most in 55 days) against only 1,782 BTC of loss; STH-SOPR hit 1.038, the highest in the series (since Oct 2025); the close was −3.22%.
findings.why: Breaking SOPR apart: versus 7 days ago, realized profit is +142% and realized loss −14%, so the rise came from profit taking, not less loss selling. CoinMetrics daily net realized P/L (all holders, 10/21) was +$604M, and +$1.885B over 7 days, more than double the prior week's +$857M, pointing the same way; the share of short-term supply in profit is 88.4% (10/21, 65.3% a week earlier), so more holders can sell at a gain. Exchange supply moved −0.02% over 7 days (10/21): no large transfers onto exchanges.
findings.alt: CheckOnChain smooths these values, so a jump from about 2,900 to 7,900 BTC in one day means the raw figure that day was very large; it could also be a large transfer counted as selling. It is one day, and CheckOnChain may revise it.
findings.history: Over the past year, "extreme realized profit on a down day" happened 4 times (3/05, 4/14, 8/22, 9/22); price 30 days later was −5.2%, +9.4%, +12.3%, −5.7%. Four cases is too few to read as a pattern; background only.
findings.so: Most short-term holders are still in profit and loss selling is low: no panic. Paper gains from the two up days were cashed in on the down day. The market stage (bull, day 14) and the exit framework are unaffected.
findings.next: Watch 10/23–10/27: does realized profit fall back below 4,000 BTC (the burst is over), and does SOPR hold above 1? A drop below 1 would mean selling turned into loss selling.

findings.title: Price fell but funding turned positive: leveraged longs are back, spot is weak
findings.lean_why: Spot demand is weak while leveraged longs add on the dip, so further drops face more long liquidations.
findings.what: Weighted funding flipped from −4.48% to +8.65% (annualized) on a −3.22% close; the 81,316 close is only +2.45% above the true market mean of 79,374 (10/16).
findings.why: All three venues turned positive: OKX +7.32%, Hyperliquid +10.95%, Deribit +2.92%, so it is not one exchange. CoinGlass shows $210M of the $222M liquidated in the 12 hours of the drop were longs, and longs kept paying as price fell: traders are buying the dip with leverage. Spot looks weak: the Coinbase premium 7-day average is −0.123%, its own 11th percentile; the provisional $525M ETF inflow on 10/21 did not hold price up.
findings.alt: Funding is a 00:05 UTC snapshot and 8.65% annualized is not extreme on its own; ETF flows and the Coinbase premium measure different buyers, and the premium only compares Coinbase with Binance. The true market mean comes from bitcoin-data and runs about 6 days behind.
findings.history: Since price fell below the true market mean on 1/31, it got back above three times (5/04, 8/26, 9/04) and each lasted only 6–9 days; this time it has stayed above since 9/19, 33 days, the longest this year (from data sampled every 3 days).
findings.so: Derivatives lean long while spot is weak, so long-liquidation pressure on dips is back; the true market mean is the nearest key level. The market stage depends on the 200-day average (still 10.5% below) and is unaffected.
findings.next: Watch whether funding stays above 5% through 10/27 and whether the Coinbase premium 7-day average gets back above 0 (spot returning would undo this reading); and whether closes hold above 79,374.
